claims.statement: The main coding agent is compiled per-run by the async factory get_agent(config) in agent/server.py, which resolves identity, sandbox, model, tools, subagents, and middleware and passes them to create_deep_agent.

The registered LangGraph 'agent' entrypoint is traced_agent, a thin wrapper produced by traced_graph_factory that calls get_agent and yields the graph inside the LangSmith tracing project 'open-swe-agent'.

get_agent returns a bare create_deep_agent with empty system prompt, no tools, no sandbox, and no middleware when there is no thread_id or the load is not for execution, gated by graph_loaded_for_execution reading the __is_for_execution__ configurable flag.
Every graph returned by get_agent sets config recursion_limit to DEFAULT_RECURSION_LIMIT (9,999), the LangGraph superstep budget for the run.

profile_login is the GitHub login of whoever sent the message that started the run (resolved via resolve_github_login) and drives authorization and credentialed integrations, which stay personal to the sender, while other settings come from the thread's own frozen settings.

get_agent obtains a cached SandboxBackendProxy for the thread with a reconnect callback that builds a LocalShellBackend for desktop runs and otherwise calls ensure_sandbox_for_thread to get-or-create a healthy thread-bound sandbox.

The agent model and effort are resolved by a precedence cascade in get_agent: team defaults, then dashboard profile overrides, then stored thread settings, then an explicit per-run agent_model_id/agent_effort that is validated against SUPPORTED_MODEL_IDS and model_supports_effort.

An explicit per-run model override is the only input allowed to move a thread off its stored settings, and the resolved settings are persisted back via store_thread_settings on non-desktop runs so later turns stay on the same model.

Chat models are built via _make_model_or_defer, which returns a deferred error model instead of raising on construction failure, so a provider misconfiguration surfaces at call time rather than failing the factory.

create_deep_agent is called with an empty system_prompt; the real prompt is rendered per-run by PrepareAgentRunMiddleware._prepare calling construct_system_prompt and stored in run state as rendered_system_prompt.
construct_system_prompt fills SYSTEM_PROMPT_TEMPLATE with per-thread main-agent sections and appends the static run-invariant OPEN_SWE_SHARED_BASE via render_open_swe_shared_base.
The base prepare middleware's awrap_model_call prepends the run-state rendered_system_prompt to the request system message on every model call and wraps the content with wrap_system_prompt.
A model turn with no tool call ends the run: the system prompt instructs the agent to call a tool every turn and nothing re-injects one, making an empty-tool turn the primary stop condition.
The agent filesystem is a CompositeBackend whose default is the sandbox backend and whose routes overlay skill and scratch paths onto other backends.

Skill routes mount bundled skills from a ReadOnly FilesystemBackend, organization and user skills from ReadOnly StoreBackends namespaced in the LangGraph store, and desktop user skills from a ReadOnly StateBackend, producing an ordered skill_sources list shared by the main agent and subagents.

On desktop runs the composite backend routes the agent's own scratch paths (/large_tool_results/ and /conversation_history/) to virtual FilesystemBackends outside the user's project so offloaded results and evicted history are not swept into git.

The tool list is curated per-run: a large static_tools set is conditionally trimmed for Slack availability, admin threads, sandbox-file-download support, and collapsed to minimal subsets for desktop and stop-summary modes.

Optional integration tools (Observability, Currents, Notion, Corridor) are registered as lazy groups in a DynamicToolMiddleware so their MCP handshake runs only when the agent asks for the group, rather than being placed in static_tools.
ExcludeToolsMiddleware removes tools that must never be exposed, using DEEP_AGENT_EXCLUDED_TOOLS (e.g. grep) or the broader STOP_SUMMARY_EXCLUDED_TOOLS in stop-summary mode.

The always-present general-purpose subagent is built by _general_purpose_subagent, reusing GENERAL_PURPOSE_SUBAGENT's name and prompt but prepending the Open SWE shared base, and is given the static tools minus background execution and minus parent-only Slack and thread tools.
A browser subagent is added to the agent only when browser tools loaded for the run.

Because subagents compile into their own graphs that parent middleware never wraps, each SubAgent spec carries its own model guards via _subagent_model_middleware (SanitizeOpenAIResponsesMiddleware and ModelCallTimeoutMiddleware).

The main agent's middleware list is ordered outermost to innermost with PrepareAgentRunMiddleware first and ModelCallTimeoutMiddleware innermost so the model-call deadline covers the provider call and a timeout escalates outward to the fallback model.
ModelCallLimitMiddleware caps model calls at MODEL_CALL_RECURSION_LIMIT (5,000) with exit_behavior 'end', ending the run when the limit is reached.
A ModelFallbackMiddleware is included only when a fallback model id is configured and differs from the primary model, so a primary model-call timeout can escalate to the fallback.

PrepareAgentRunMiddleware is checkpointed per-run setup that latches run_prepared_for so resumed attempts of the same invocation skip completed setup, and its _prepare must be idempotent because a run that fails before the checkpoint re-executes setup.
get_agent is the single customization seam for forking Open SWE, choosing the sandbox provider, model, tools, subagents, and middleware consumed by create_deep_agent.
